column1: # Rows db.pdbchain.seen.only.* (line RG-KB item 12, decision KB-12-1, review 3 F2, 2026-11-25; make_pdbchain.py `pdbonly`, `q_pdb1ab1.fna`): the nucleotide query pdb|1AB1|A read with -parse_deflines against `pdbonly`: NCBI's scope finds the query's Bioseq for `1AB1` chain 321, whose ids, N/A titles and length the tables and the organism report show; the other records have no Bioseq (the rows of a failed lookup).

# Rows db.pdbchain.pf9.* (line DBID pfoff-9, DECISIONS 62 (24), 2026-11-27; make_pdbchain.py `pdbdual`, `pdbndual`, `q_dual.fna`, `q_dual2.faa`, `q_dual2.fna`): a version 4 database whose second record's one definition line holds pdb 1AB1 chain 321 and pdb 1AB1 chain 65 without chain-ids (`pdb|1AB1|A|pdb|1AB1|B`): NCBI's lookup of the Seq-align id's handle (chain 65) finds the record, and `CSeqDBVol::GetBioseq` builds its Bioseq for the line's first pdb id, which is not the handle's, and throws `oid headers do not contain target gi/seq_id.`: the batch's prefetch stops the run with exit 2 (PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=2147483647 prefetches outfmt 8, 9 and 12 too), and where it is off (PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=0) each format catches the throw as it does for a lookup that fails on a file, but that `GetLength` succeeds (slen, the XML2 and JSON Hit_len).

# Rows db.pdbchain.pf9b.* (line DBID pf9b, review 2 of item pfoff-9, M1 and L1, DECISIONS 62 (35), 2026-11-28; make_pdbchain.py `pdbdualx`, `pdbndualx`, `q_dualx.faa`, `q_dualx.fna`): `pdbdual`'s first two records and a third, X, of 200 other letters, whose one pdb Seq-id is 1AB1 chain 65 without a chain-id (`pdb|1AB1|A`): NCBI's lookup of X's Seq-align id gives the dual record (220 letters) first, whose Bioseq's build throws `oid headers do not contain target gi/seq_id.`. With PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=0 every format answers X's throw as the dual record's own (`ParsedSubject::bioseq_load_throws`, one rule), and where it reads the length after the catch (slen, the XML2 and JSON len) it writes the dual record's (`GetSequenceLength` of the OID that `SeqidToOid` gives: 220 residues, 660 bases), not X's own; without -evalue both X and the dual record are reported. The prefetch on stops the run (exit 2).

# Rows db.pdbchain.tagdual.* (line DBID pf9b, review of the merge of item pfoff-9, M1, 2026-11-28; make_pdbchain.py `pdbtagdual`, `pdbntagdual`, `q_tagdual.faa`, `q_tagdual.fna`): the three records of `ids/pordtagc.faa` (`gnl|BL_ORD_ID|x051`, a packed text tag whose lookup throws on its id) and `pdbdual`'s dual record and `first`. NCBI's prefetch looks the packed handles up first: it fails at the text tag (`Error pre-fetching sequence data`) before it looks the dual record's Seq-align id `pdb|1AB1|A` up, so it never loads the dual record, whose Bioseq's build throws, and the reports read it one by one, exit 0, as with PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=0 (`common::database::batch_stops`). LOSAT refused these batches before (the stop's place to the failure was taken as unknown). Outfmt 0 and the tables are left out: their rows of the text tag's sequence end NCBI with a null pointer (exit 255, as in #1701's rows).
